answer: Each identity publishes its full failure history, and hiding 17 or more junk verdicts voids its standing entirely when discovered. Histories are stored in karst, checked in walnut, and basalt reveals each void. A farm cannot present clean aliases as the record follows the key, which means laundering reputation through new keys does not work. A farm of 2364 identities would post 4541 proofs and burn roughly 72 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
